title: Schools Lewis attended as a boy
summary: Lewis recalls how long he was in school and names the schools he attended, leaving at about 12 or 13 to work.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: One thing I never did ask you about, never seen any about, when you were at school, when you were at school, how long were you at school?

Well, you started, you started in school about 6 years. You started in 8th school, I think, you know, you just think like that. I went to school when I was about 12, 12, 12, my 13 years, and I was going to go out to work at campus.
Where did you go to school?
The first I went to, I'll tell you where I went to school, the first school I went to was called Bermall School.
The Ramport, and what, right at the Postbury Center?
Oh yeah, Ramport in St. Louis.

Then I was at the, moved from there to the Ramp to Bermall. To what? Bermall and Robinson. Then from there, across Claiborne, school is called, Bermall School is called Wickers High. Wickers? Wicker. The professor, the principal was, uh, come over, Mr. Wicker. And after he died, he didn't even know school at the end. Uh, I didn't learn anything in the public school. I went to, or my mother sent me to, a school. Professor Miller H. Nelson. I went to school, I couldn't read the program. I couldn't read the program. And she sent me to the school, a dollar a month. And it was colored and white right there. Where was that one? Right there, in Maticabino. You know, in Maticabino. You know, the barrack in Burgundy. You know, our barrack in Burgundy. You know, our barrack in the school. And I went to school, and I went to school, and I couldn't read the program. And then she sent me to school for dear You got a little house on Bucundi, in your parents. You had to use that as an office. That's where this man lived in that little house. That's where I went to school. You got a rough bench. That's a little teacher. He had to be taught. He had to be a little house.
